# `pi_station_scan`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Scan for nearby Wi-Fi networks that the device could join as a station.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe4510, ns_net::pi_station_scan @0x702ac0 (64-bit build) |

Runs the network script's scan branch, which asks the Wi-Fi supplicant to start a radio scan and then reads the results; this is an active scan, not a cached list. The reply is an array of networks, or {value: array} when ret_obj is true. Only networks in the same band as the device's own access point are listed, one entry per SSID (the strongest), with signal level in dBm at or above -80. Blocks until the script completes.

Side effects: Initiates an active radio scan through the supplicant tool and logs the command, synchronously with no timeout.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"pi_station_scan"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object\|array\|boolean\|integer\|null | no | - | Optional. An object with ret_obj, or a positional [boolean-or-integer]. Absent, null or any unrecognised container behaves as defaults; there is no error for malformed ret_obj. No scan-control keys are read. [READ] |
| `params.ret_obj` | boolean\|integer | no | False | Wrap the reply array as {value: array}. Boolean or integer (0 false, nonzero true). A malformed value is silently treated as false. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 214 | The scan script process could not be started | `fail to run command` |
| 223 | Scan script produced empty output | `no result from command` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Other propagated failure codes are unresolved. The app (3.3.2) passes null params to its sender; whether the member is then omitted on the wire is not established.

## Example

Request, default:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"pi_station_scan"}
```

Request, wrapped - Object-wrapped reply:

```json
{"id":82,"method":"pi_station_scan","params":{"ret_obj":true}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_scan","result":[{"freq":2437,"sig_lev":-52,"flags":"[WPA2-PSK-CCMP][ESS]","ssid":"ExampleNet"}],"code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, ok-wrapped-empty:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_scan","result":{"value":[]},"code":0,"id":82}
```

Reply, no-output:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"pi_station_scan","error":"no result from command","code":223,"id":83}
```
